title: Relative colimits in a fiber tested by all local transports
statement: Use quasicategories, coherent functors, colimits and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], relative colimit diagrams and right join cones of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], and inner and cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $q:E\to S$ be an inner fibration of quasicategories such that its pullback along each edge $a:\Delta^1\to S$ is a cocartesian fibration. For a vertex $s$ put $E_s=E\times_S\{s\}$. For an edge $a:s\to t$, a transport functor for $a$ is a functor $a_!:E_s\to E_t$ for which there is a simplicial map $H:E_s\times\Delta^1\to E\times_{S,a}\Delta^1$ over $\Delta^1$ with $H|_{E_s\times\{0\}}$ the inclusion, $H|_{E_s\times\{1\}}=a_!$, and every edge $H|_{\{x\}\times\Delta^1}$ cocartesian for the edge pullback. Let $K$ be any small simplicial set and $c:K^{\triangleright}\to E_s$ any diagram. For a diagram $u:K^{\triangleright}\to E_t$ with cone vertex $v$, its induced coherent cocone $u|_K\to\Delta_Ku(v)$ is the precomposition of $u$ with the map $K\times\Delta^1\to K^{\triangleright}$ that sends a simplex $(\sigma,\alpha)$, $\alpha:[n]\to[1]$, to the join simplex whose initial block is $\sigma$ restricted to $\alpha^{-1}(0)$ and whose final block is $\alpha^{-1}(1)$ at the cone vertex. Then the composite $K^{\triangleright}\xrightarrow{c}E_s\hookrightarrow E$ is a $q$-colimit diagram if and only if, for every edge $a:s\to t$ of $S$ and every transport functor $a_!$ for $a$, the induced coherent cocone of $a_!c$ is colimiting in $E_t$. Degenerate edges are included. No other colimits are assumed; neither global cocartesian lifts nor coherence of transports under composition is assumed. All objects lie in a fixed sufficiently large universe.

source.place: Higher Topos Theory, Proposition 4.3.1.10 and its proof, printed pp. 265-266 (PDF pp. 283-284). Read online 2026-10-17. No Stacks Project tag states this quasicategorical criterion. WANTED: archived HTT in literature/.

proof.text: Write $p=q$, $\mathcal E=E$, $\mathcal B=S$, and $b=s$ for the data of the statement. Put $a=c|_K$, $x=c(*)$, and let $\alpha:a\to\Delta_Kx$ be the induced coherent cocone. Every strict fiber is a quasicategory: an inner-horn problem in the fiber lifts against $p$ over the constant base simplex. Fix an edge $f:b\to b'$ and put $\mathcal E_f=\mathcal E\times_{\mathcal B,f}\Delta^1$, with projection $p_f$. By hypothesis $p_f$ is a cocartesian fibration; in particular it is an inner fibration, and $\mathcal E_f$ is a quasicategory, since an inner-horn problem in $\mathcal E_f$ is solved first in the quasicategory $\Delta^1$ and then lifted against $p_f$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] to $p_f$, so its horn-cocartesian edges satisfy the mapping-space hypothesis of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport]. All uses of that transport theorem below are for $p_f$, over $\Delta^1$. Transport functors exist: apply its diagram-lifting assertion to the inclusion $\mathcal E_b\to\mathcal E_f$ over the constant $0$ diagram and the constant transformation $0\to1$, in a containing universe. The resulting endpoint lies in $\mathcal E_{b'}$ and its lifting cylinder is a witness of the kind required in the statement. For any specified transport functor $f_!$ and its witness $H$, set $c_f=f_!c$ and $\lambda=H\circ(c\times\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^1})$. The componentwise assertion of the same theorem, for shape $K^{\triangleright}$, makes $\lambda:c\to c_f$ cocartesian over the constant $0\to1$ transformation for $\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\triangleright},p_f)$. Its boundary $\lambda_a$ and apex $\lambda_x$ are likewise cocartesian for $\operatorname{Fun}(K,p_f)$ and $p_f$. Write $a_f,x_f,\alpha_f$ for the boundary, apex and coherent cocone of $c_f$. These are restrictions of this one cylinder; no global cocartesian property of $p$ is asserted.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1.10, proof: first pull back along the chosen edge, then choose a cocartesian transformation of the entire cocone.

proof.text:
By [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test], $c$ is a $p$-colimit diagram if and only if, for every $z\in\mathcal E$, the apex square is a homotopy pullback. Write $s=pz$ and abbreviate its four corners by
$$U_z=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,z),\quad V_z=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)}(a,\Delta_Kz),\quad S_z=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(b,s),\quad W_z=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal B)}(\Delta_Kb,\Delta_Ks).$$
The top map sends $u$ to $\Delta_K(u)\alpha$. Since $c$ lies in a strict fiber, $p\alpha$ is the identity coherent transformation of $\Delta_Kb$, so the bottom map is exactly $\delta:S_z\to W_z$, $f\mapsto\Delta_K f$. All these are spaces and the square includes its specified coherent commutativity, as required by that node.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1.10, reduction to outgoing-arrow tests; Kerodon 7.1.6.19 (02X1), colimit dual and apex formulation.

proof.text:
Form the path pullback $P_z=V_z\times^h_{W_z}S_z$ of step 2 and its projection to $S_z$. It is Kan by [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison]. The apex square is a homotopy pullback exactly when its specified comparison $\Phi_z:U_z\to P_z$ is a weak equivalence. Apply [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] over $\mathrm{id}_{S_z}$: this is equivalent to equivalence on every homotopy fiber over a vertex $f\in S_z$.
To compute the target fiber without choosing compositions of simplicial paths, use the replacement clause of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]: factor $V_z\to W_z$ as $V_z\xrightarrow{\sim}\widetilde V_z\twoheadrightarrow W_z$. The replacement represents $P_z$ by $Q_z=\widetilde V_z\times_{W_z}S_z$, naturally with both projections. Its projection to $S_z$ is a Kan fibration: solve a horn in the first coordinate using the fibration to $W_z$ and the prescribed simplex in $S_z$. Thus $Q_z$ is Kan. The same replacement represents $\operatorname{hofib}_{\Delta_Kf}(V_z\to W_z)$ by $\widetilde V_z\times_{W_z}\{\Delta_Kf\}$. This is exactly the strict fiber of $Q_z\to S_z$ over $f$ by the degreewise pullback formula; strict and homotopy fibers agree by [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison]. Naturality of replacement and fiber detection carry the specified comparison to
$$\operatorname{hofib}_f(U_z\to S_z)\longrightarrow\operatorname{hofib}_{\Delta_Kf}(V_z\to W_z).$$
Consequently the apex square is a homotopy pullback precisely when all these fiber maps are equivalences. Empty $S_z$ is allowed by fiber detection.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1.10, mapping-space reconstruction of the edgewise test; the existing Kan-Quillen replacement clause computes the iterated fiber by strict pullback associativity.

proof.text:
Fix $z\in\mathcal E_{b'}$ and $f:b\to b'$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-edge-pullback-mapping-fiber] to $p$, once with shape $\Delta^0$ and objects $x,z$, and once with shape $K$ and diagrams $a,\Delta_Kz$. It identifies the two homotopy fibers in step 3 with
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E_f}(x,z),\qquad\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E_f)}(a,\Delta_Kz).$$
Its naturality clause carries the fiber comparison to $u\mapsto\Delta_K(u)\alpha$ in $\mathcal E_f$.
Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] to $p_f$ and the lifts $\lambda_x,\lambda_a$ from step 1. Their base mapping spaces are $\operatorname{Map}_{\Delta^1}(0,1)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\Delta^1)}(\Delta_K0,\Delta_K1)$; both are the one-point Kan complex by clause (2) of the edge-pullback lemma (including its $K=\Delta^0$ case). Hence its homotopy-fiber formulas give equivalences, by precomposition,
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E_{b'}}(x_f,z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E_f}(x,z),\qquad\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E_{b'})}(a_f,\Delta_Kz)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E_f)}(a,\Delta_Kz).$$
These are applications inside the cocartesian edge pullback, whose target strict fiber is $\mathcal E_{b'}$; they require no global cocartesian lifts for $p$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1.10, reduction to the edge pullback and comparison after a cocartesian transformation; the ambient-to-local mapping-space comparison uses the existing edge-pullback mapping-fiber and pointwise cocartesian transport statements.

proof.text:
The single cylinder $\lambda=H(c\times\mathrm{id})$ also identifies the comparison maps, not just their source and target spaces. Restrict it along $(K\times\Delta^1)\times\Delta^1\to K^{\triangleright}\times\Delta^1$, where the first interval is the stated join-collapse map and the second is the transport interval. Its four sides are $\alpha,\alpha_f,\lambda_a,\Delta_K\lambda_x$, so it supplies the coherent square
$$\alpha_f\lambda_a\simeq\Delta_K(\lambda_x)\alpha.$$
For $v:x_f\to z$, postcompose this square with $\Delta_Kv$. Thus the comparison $u\mapsto\Delta_K(u)\alpha$ of step 4 corresponds, under the two precomposition equivalences there, to
$$\beta_{f,z}:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E_{b'}}(x_f,z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E_{b'})}(a_f,\Delta_Kz),\qquad v\mapsto\Delta_K(v)\alpha_f.$$
All higher simplices are retained because the square is the restriction of the actual two-parameter cylinder. The two vertical maps are equivalences, so the step-3 fiber map is an equivalence if and only if $\beta_{f,z}$ is. This holds for each specified witness $H$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1.10, proof: choose a cocartesian transformation of the entire right cone; its boundary/apex naturality is restriction of that cylinder.

proof.text: Assume first that every $f_!c$ is colimiting. For any $z\in\mathcal E$ and any $f:b\to pz$, apply the cocone mapping-space criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] in the quasicategory $\mathcal E_{pz}$. It makes $\beta_{f,z}$ a weak equivalence, since $c_f$ is the specified transported colimit cocone. Steps 3-5 then make the apex square for this $z$ a homotopy pullback. This holds for all $z$, so step 2 proves that $c$ is a $p$-colimit diagram.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1.10, implication from all transported colimits to a relative colimit.

proof.text: Conversely suppose $c$ is a $p$-colimit diagram. Steps 2-5 show that $\beta_{f,z}$ is a weak equivalence whenever $f:b\to pz$. Fix $b'$ and an edge $f:b\to b'$, and let $z$ vary over every object of $\mathcal E_{b'}$. These are exactly the maps $\beta_{f,z}$ required by the dual cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], so $c_f=f_!c$ is a colimit in that fiber. The quantifier includes the degenerate edge at $b$. For $K=\varnothing$, $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E_s)$ is the one-point category, so the very same criterion says each $x_f$ is initial; for $K=\Delta^0$ it says the transported cocone edge is an equivalence. Neither direction has assumed any colimit besides the particular $c_f$, nor weak contractibility of $K$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1.10, reverse implication, with the identity and empty-shape cases explicit.
